unit: kWh per year, maximum energy use when new
volume_basis: AV is the total adjusted volume in cubic feet as defined by the DOE test procedure appendices, computed from the fresh-food and freezer compartment volumes. It is not the total refrigerated volume printed on most labels; for a refrigerator-freezer AV is larger. Whoever calls standard_ceiling must pass AV, or accept and label the difference.
rounding: 10 CFR 430.32(a) rounds each standard to the nearest kWh per year, rounding a halfway value up.
scope: Refrigerators and refrigerator-freezers up to 39 cubic feet. Freezer classes are left out on purpose. Units manufactured before 1993-01-01 have no entry here and get no ceiling. Compact classes 11 to 15 use the 1993 equations of the matching full-size class for units made before 2001-07-01, as footnote a of the 2004 table says. Class names are stored per period because the wording changed: from 2001-07-01 to 2014-09-14, class 3 also covers all-refrigerators with automatic defrost (class 3A from 2014-09-15), and class 1 also covers manual-defrost all-refrigerators (class 1A from 2014-09-15).
